summary: 403 ERR · 30B markdown · stealthy · one HTTP attempt is bound by the learned ceiling for this host (it answers pages fast, so the tier gives it 5000ms, not your 25000ms) — a per-host habit, not a cap you set · this call makes 1 extra direct request to the target before the browser runs: a liveness probe (direct, 3s, no retries, no synthetic headers, no redirect hop). Your service's own log will show that one next to the browser's navigation - it is dhole dialing, not the page. · the target is loopback/private, so the browser tier navigated without dhole's invented google referer. What that browser sends of its own (UA, `sec-ch-ua*`, `sec-fetch-*`) arrived as it always does, plus every header you named · http_error_403: server returned error status · redirected from http://127.0.0.1:8399/challenge/text to http://127.0.0.1:8399/challenge/verify
next_action: access denied (HTTP 403) - the site is refusing this client. the browser tier already made this request (fetcher_used='stealthy') and the site refused it the same way - rendering is not the untried lever here. Switch source, or re-call later if the refusal looks session-dependent. the page reads as: http_error_403: server returned error status. That is about the content, not about this call: `metadata.actions` holds the receipts of the chain that ran. Do not re-issue the same chain - every step already marked ok would run again.
